title: Who Was I Becoming?
headline: What Difficult People Reveal About Your Heart
headline_sub: Who Was I Becoming While Interacting With Them?
tagline: Your hardest relationships often become God’s greatest classroom for Christlike character.
seo_title: What Difficult People Reveal About You: Colossians 3:12-13 | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Sometimes difficult people don't expose what's wrong with them; they expose what still needs transformation in us. An audit for men from Colossians 3:12-13.
verse_text: Clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience. Bear with each other and forgive one another….

scriptures.text: Clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience. Bear with each other and forgive one another….

items: This week’s audit isn’t measuring how good you’ve been.
It’s revealing what your heart has been seeing.
Jesus said, “Every healthy tree bears good fruit.”
Fruit always reveals the health of the root.
If irritation has become your default response….
don’t merely ask, “How can I become more patient?”
Ask, “What has my heart been looking at this week?”
Because whatever captures our attention…. eventually shapes our affection.
Our affection shapes our perception.
Our perception shapes our relationships.

blocks.text: Perhaps the greatest question isn’t, “Was that person difficult?”
The greater question is: “Who was I becoming while interacting with them?”

items: Do I show patience toward others?
Do I assume the best before assuming the worst?
Do I treat people with dignity regardless of how they treat me?
Do I become easily irritated when inconvenienced?
Do I genuinely seek to understand before being understood?
Do I see people through God’s perspective rather than my own preferences?
Who frustrated me most this week?
Did I treat them as an obstacle…. or an image-bearer?
What did that interaction reveal about my own heart?
How might Jesus have seen and responded to that same person?
Sometimes difficult people don’t expose what’s wrong with them.
They expose what still needs transformation in us.
The Holy Spirit often uses difficult relationships as a mirror.
Not to shame us….
but to show us where He is still forming Christ within us.
Fruit isn’t manufactured.
Fruit is cultivated through remaining in the Vine.
Your hardest relationships often become God’s greatest classroom for Christlike character.
The people who reveal your impatience may also become the people through whom Christ teaches you His compassion.
